Convert a 3D panel to an rgl mesh or rgl scene

Source: R/export-bridges.R
rgl-bridge-3d.Rd

as.mesh3d() returns the scene of one panel as one rgl mesh3d object with vertex colours, ready for rgl::shade3d(), rgl::writeOBJ() or other mesh tools. plot3d() draws the panel in an rgl window with rgl's own triangles, segments, points and text, viewed from the plot's camera. Coordinates are model coordinates with the vertical axis of the plot as +z; see export_3d().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ggplot3d'
as.mesh3d(
  x,
  panel = 1L,
  furniture = FALSE,
  lines = c("tube", "line"),
  points = c("mesh", "point"),
  size = 1,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  dpi = 96,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'ggplot3d'
plot3d(
  x,
  panel = 1L,
  furniture = FALSE,
  size = 1,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  dpi = 96,
  add = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A ggplot with coord_3d().

panel, furniture, size, width, height, dpi

See export_3d().

lines, points

See export_3d(). "line" and "point" fill the mesh's segment (is) and point (ip) indices.

...

Unused.

add

Whether to draw into the current rgl scene instead of a new one, default FALSE.

Value

as.mesh3d(): a mesh3d object. plot3d(): the rgl object ids, invisibly.

Details

Faces drawn with lighting in the plot are drawn lit by rgl; all other geometry is unlit. Line widths and point sizes are converted to pixels at dpi. rgl centres the view on the bounding box of the drawn geometry, so the view matches the plot's camera angles and projection but can differ in framing.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("rgl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 10), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 10))
  d$z <- d$x * exp(-d$x^2 - d$y^2)
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
    geom_surface_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = z)) + coord_3d()
  old <- options(rgl.useNULL = TRUE)
  rgl::plot3d(p)
  rgl::close3d()
  options(old)
  mesh <- rgl::as.mesh3d(p)
  dim(mesh$it)
}
